newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Leumi Insurance begins trading on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Leumi Insurance begins trading on Sunday.

text.p: Israel's Leumi Insurance Holdings Ltd, spun off from Africa Israel Investments Ltd in order to be sold to Italy's Assicurazioni Generali SpA, begins trading on the stock exchange on Sunday.

Some 25 percent of the company will be traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) at an opening price of 128.56 agorot, or a market valuation of 1.3 billion shekels. It will be traded in the TASE's mishtanim framework.
The price represents 30.13 percent of Africa Israel's weighted share price, the day before Africa Israel's Leumi Insurance shares were distributed to Africa Israel shareholders on January 8.
Generali simultaneously swapped shares it held in Leumi Insurance's main subsidiary Migdal for shares in the parent company.
Bank Leumi now holds about 44 percent of Leumi Insurance and Generali about 27 percent.

Generali is committed to making a general offer for 42 percent of the public's and Bank Leumi's shares, which a source close to the offering said would probably occur sometime before the end of February.
The offer will be made at a company valuation of about 3.2 billion shekels, or about 3.123 shekels a share.

With the completion of the offering, Generali will become the controlling shareholder in Leumi Insurance, completing a transaction the two companies agreed on last year. Bank Leumi, will be left with no more than 25 percent of Leumi Insurance.

Like the other comercial banks, Leumi was forced to reduce its holdings in non-bank companies as part of bank-reform legislation implemented by the government in 1996. The law requires Bank Leumi to reduce its holding by another five percent, which will be done by selling further shares to Generali before the deadline.
The bank arranged to spin off Leumi Insurance from Africa Israel in order to sell the two companies separately.

Market analysts expect Leumi Insurance's share price to rise sharply in trading, although not to the full value Generali has put on the company. One analyst estimated Leumi Insurance's market capitalisation would reach about 2.3 billion shekels.
Africa Israel shares, meanwhile, fell 30-35 percent in the two days after the Leumi Insurance distribution, erasing some some 1.1 billion shekels from its market capitalisation.
